model.proposal: Narrow federal Title VII gender-identity enforcement through a biological-sex interpretation and rescission of EEOC guidance.
model.claimed_authority: Executive policy direction, EEOC guidance authority, and litigation positions under Title VII.
model.baseline: Title VII statutory text, Bostock controlling precedent, and the 2024 EEOC harassment guidance.
model.required_instrument: Executive direction plus agency action, litigation, or both; the Supreme Court holding cannot be erased by agency guidance alone.

implementation_chain.actor: State of Texas and Heritage Foundation

implementation_chain.event: The challenged guidance categories are vacated.
Agency rescission is reported; complete meeting record remains an open source item.

observed_evidence: EO 14168 official text is primary-verified in the source ledger.
Texas v. EEOC memorandum opinion and order is primary-verified in the source ledger.
Bostock is independently primary-verified in the state-inventory upgrade.
The January 2026 EEOC meeting record remains not independently retrieved.
jurisdictional_variation: State statutory and interpretive protections vary and are incompletely verified state by state.
Federal private Title VII litigation remains separately available under the bounded source record.
response_pathways: Independent state nondiscrimination statutes and state human-rights enforcement.
State or local responses where not preempted.
timing_dependencies: Appellate status of Texas v. EEOC.
Availability of the complete January 2026 EEOC meeting record.
unresolved_questions: Actual nationwide charge-processing effect is not quantified.
The source pack does not prove that Bostock itself has been overruled or narrowed beyond the identified guidance categories.

model.proposal: State removal of gender-identity protection followed by preemption of broader local nondiscrimination categories.
model.claimed_authority: Iowa General Assembly authority to amend state civil-rights law and define local-government authority.
model.baseline: Iowa Civil Rights Act protection for gender identity beginning in 2007 and local authority to maintain broader protections.
model.required_instrument: Enacted state legislation amending the protected-class definition and a later state-local preemption clause.

implementation_chain.event: SF 418 removes gender identity from the state protected-class structure, effective July 1, 2025.
SF 579 preempts broader or different local discrimination categories in 2026.

observed_evidence: SF 418 enacted text and legislative history are primary-verified in the current dossier.
SF 579 outcome and legislative history are secondary-verified.
SF 579 exact clause and signing date are secondary-verified at high confidence.
Complete enrolled SF 579 text has not been reviewed line by line.
jurisdictional_variation: The current source says 13 cities plus unincorporated Johnson County had local gender-identity protections.
The broader preemption-family mechanism predates Project 2025 and appears in different states through different vehicles.
response_pathways: Federal Title VII private litigation remains available under the bounded source record.
State constitutional litigation is theoretical until a filing or opinion is retrieved.
Local implementation responses after preemption remain unestablished.
timing_dependencies: Effective dates in the enacted state laws.
Any state or federal challenge to SF 418 or SF 579.
unresolved_questions: Complete enrolled SF 579 text not independently read line by line.
Litigation status not established from a retrieved filing or opinion.

relationships.evidence_note: Shared framing, temporal proximity, and stated alignment do not prove coordination with Project 2025 or the White House.
The state and federal mechanisms act through different sovereign authorities and implementation instruments.
